featured_reviews.name: Atanu M
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Banana Leaf Restaurant at Palladium, Phoenix Mall. The restaurant has a pleasant ambiance with comfortable seating and a clean, well-maintained dining area. The menu offers a good selection of South Indian dishes, and the food quality was impressive. The dishes were freshly prepared, flavorful, and served in generous portions. The authentic taste and quality ingredients made the meal enjoyable, and it is evident that the kitchen puts effort into maintaining consistency.

Unfortunately, the service did not live up to the quality of the food. While the staff members were polite and courteous, the overall service was noticeably slow. From taking orders to attending to requests, there were significant delays throughout the meal. What was particularly disappointing was that we had to repeatedly ask for basic necessities such as water, extra plates, cutlery, and other table requirements. These are things that should ideally be provided proactively, especially in a restaurant located in a premium destination like Palladium, Phoenix Mall.

The restaurant has great potential because the food is genuinely good and worth recommending. However, the dining experience was affected by the lack of attentiveness and the need to constantly remind the staff about simple requests. Better coordination among the service team and a more customer-focused approach would make a substantial difference.

Overall, Banana Leaf delivers excellent food with authentic flavors, making it a good choice for South Indian cuisine lovers. However, improvements in service speed and attention to detail are needed for the experience to match the quality of the food. I would visit again for the food, but I hope the service standards improve in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Ayush Bhandari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a spot where traditional South Indian soul meets a modern, aesthetic vibe, Malgudi in Lower Parel is a masterclass in culinary harmony. Curated by the legendary Shankar Mahadevan, the restaurant feels less like a typical eatery and more like a carefully composed melody—vibrant, comforting, and full of character.
The ambience hits you first; it’s thoughtfully designed with a clean, aesthetic appeal that makes it perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch or a stylish dinner.
The Food: From Classic to Creative
The menu takes you on a journey through Karnataka and beyond, elevating humble staples into gourmet experiences.
Podi Cheese Balls: The spice of the podi cuts through the richness of the cheese, creating a crunchy, gooey delight that’s hard to stop at just one.
Ghee Podi Thate Idli: This was a standout. The idli was incredibly soft, acting as the perfect canvas for the fragrant, nutty podi and a generous dousing of ghee.
Davangere Benne Podi Dosa: True to its roots, this dosa was buttery (*benne*) and crisp, with the podi adding a layer of depth that reminded us why this regional specialty is so iconic.
Mulbagal Legacy Cheese Masala Dosa: The addition of cheese modernized the legacy recipe without overshadowing the traditional masala. Beverages:
Mango Berry Matcha: A vibrant, fruity twist on matcha that felt light and refreshing—a great palate cleanser between the buttery dosas.
Coconut Cold Brew Coffee: Smooth and tropical. The natural sweetness of the coconut milk paired beautifully with the bold kick of the cold brew.
Desserts:
You cannot leave without trying the Filter Kaffi Panna Cotta. It’s a brilliant nod to South Indian coffee culture, with a silky texture and a deep caffeine punch. The Chocolate Pull-Up Cake added a bit of "Instagrammable" drama to the table—decadent, rich, and the perfect end for any chocolate lover.

Malgudi isn't just about the name behind it; the food truly speaks for itself. It captures the "Legacy" of South India while dressing it up for the modern Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: VlogWithFurkan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited SpiceKlub to explore their newly launched menu, and it was truly an impressive experience for anyone who enjoys modern Indian fusion cuisine.
We started with their appetizers, and the Masala Pav Bagel Bites were an absolute highlight. It’s a creative take on Mumbai’s classic masala pav, served inside sesame bagels with a perfect balance of spiced onion-tomato masala, buttery chutney, and cream cheese. The flavours felt familiar yet completely elevated.
The Desi Hummus Dip was another standout dish. Unlike regular hummus, this one blends creamy chickpea hummus with bold, smoky Pindi chole flavours. The crunchy toppings and spiced oil drizzle added great texture and depth, making it a must-try for fusion lovers.
For beverages, we tried the Jamun Sour and Kanji Martini. The Jamun Sour was refreshing, tangy, and well-balanced with a hint of citrus, while the Kanji Martini offered a unique fermented flavour with mustard and kala namak notes — definitely something different and worth experiencing.
In the main course, the Hyderabadi Chilli Roast was beautifully executed. Stuffed green chillies filled with herbed goat cheese paired perfectly with the rich peanut, sesame, and coconut-based salan, offering a great balance of spice and creaminess.
The most unique part of the experience was the Bubbling Kulfi. It’s served at an extreme temperature and cannot be eaten directly, making it an interactive dessert where you mix it with add-ons before enjoying. A fun and innovative concept that stands out.
Overall, SpiceKlub truly delivers when it comes to creativity, presentation, and flavour. It’s the perfect place for anyone looking to try something different from the usual dining options in Mumbai. Highly recommended for fusion food lovers!

featured_reviews.name: Mishti Khadye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ishara – A must-visit for food + vibe + meaning

Ambience: Absolutely beautiful. The restaurant has different seating areas so it never feels cramped, and when I visited there was live music that added to the whole experience. Great spot for a relaxed dinner with friends or a date.

Staff & Philosophy:What stood out most was the staff. Everyone was incredibly friendly and accommodating. Ishara operates on a philosophy I really respect — they hire staff for their unique abilities like deep focus, intuition, and warmth, rather than focusing on disabilities. You don’t need to know sign language at all; the floor managers are there to help and make communication smooth. It made the service feel warm and personal.

What we ordered
1. Virgin Mojito – Refreshing and spot on.
2. Mushroom Galawat Kebab– Must try!A vegetarian galouti kebab that’s super soft, melts in your mouth, and is packed with flavor.
3. Lobster Malai– Rich and creamy.
4. Dilli Papdi Chaat– Light, fresh, and a good palate cleanser.
5. Black Pepper Chicken Tikka– Tender, creamy, and juicy.
6. Moplah Chemeen Biryani (Prawn Biryani)– _Must try main course._ Cooked with coconut milk and mild spices, the prawns were juicy and flavorful. It’s not your typical biryani — the rice is a bit mushy, but it works perfectly with the dish.
7. Rasmalai Tres Leches– A fusion that leans more traditional rasmalai. Rich, and easily shareable for 2 people.
8. Baklava– Flaky, fresh, with pista layered in between. Even better with vanilla ice cream.

I also tried a few dishes from their Karavalli Festival menu, and everything maintained the same quality. You can tell they put care into the food here.

Overall: Great experience from start to finish. The food, ambience, and the story behind the place make it worth visiting.

Tip: Book reservations in advance, especially on weekends and holidays — it gets packed fast. Also check Swiggy, Zomato, and Dineout for discounts before you go.

Follow me on IG for the video review at @itsmishtikhadye

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Ishaara at Palladium recently and it turned out to be a memorable dining experience—not just for the food, but for the overall concept and service.

The ambience is elegant yet calming, with a minimalistic design that allows you to relax and enjoy your meal without too much noise or distraction. It feels premium but still comfortable enough for a casual outing.

What really stands out is their unique service model, where the staff communicates through sign language. Despite that, the service is extremely smooth, attentive, and warm. You genuinely feel the effort and hospitality, which adds a special emotional value to the experience.

Coming to the food, we tried a variety of dishes:

* Nihari Soup – Deep, rich, and full of flavour. A great start to the meal, especially if you enjoy slow-cooked, meaty broths.
* Chicken Roll – Nicely done, with good balance of spices and texture. Simple but satisfying.
* Palak Paneer Kofta – Soft koftas with a creamy spinach gravy, slightly on the indulgent side but very comforting.
* Mutton Champaran – One of the highlights. Well-cooked, aromatic, and packed with bold spices. You can taste the slow cooking in every bite.
* Dindigul Biryani – Fragrant with a mild tangy note, distinct from regular biryanis. Well-layered and flavourful without being too heavy.

The menu beautifully brings together regional Indian flavours, and each dish feels thoughtfully prepared rather than overly commercial.

If I had to point out anything, it would be that portion sizes could feel slightly moderate for the price point—but the quality and experience make up for it.

Overall, Ishaara is not just about dining—it’s about experiencing food with purpose. Great food, meaningful service, and a peaceful ambience make it worth visiting.
